mechanics.name: Ghost Notes
mechanics.currentEffect: While you are Exhausted, your Scratch Marks disappear 50% faster and your Exhaustion recovery rate increases by 5/7.5/10%. Ghost Notes does not itself cause Exhaustion.
activation: You must be suffering from the Exhausted status effect.
Ends/deactivates when: The effects stop when Exhausted ends.
mechanics.patchNote: Latest live balance change (9.2.0): Introduced; no later material live balance change located in the official notes checked.
mechanics.plainEnglishSummary: While Exhausted, you recover from it faster and your Scratch Marks fade faster.
duration: Applies for as long as you are Exhausted.
specialInteractions: Ghost Notes does not inflict Exhausted; it only affects an existing Exhausted status.

editorial.summary: While Exhausted, Scratch Marks disappear 50% faster and Exhaustion recovers up to 10% faster.
useCases: Pair with any Exhaustion perk to shorten downtime slightly.
Make trail tracking less reliable during the same period you are waiting for Exhaustion to recover.
Add passive value without changing activation habits.
counters: Does nothing while you are not Exhausted.
The 10% recovery increase is much smaller than Vigil.
Only changes Scratch-Mark duration, not Blood, sound, or Aura reading.
cons: Requires another perk or effect to cause Exhaustion.
Usually worse than Vigil as pure Exhaustion support.
analysis: Ghost Notes lands at this position because it is a nice companion perk rather than a build centerpiece. While Exhausted, it slightly shortens the recovery period and makes Scratch Marks disappear much faster.

The stealth half is often more interesting than the recovery number. Fifty percent faster Scratch-Mark disappearance can make long chase transitions harder to read, particularly after an Exhaustion burst creates enough distance to break line of sight.
The problem is efficiency. Ten percent faster Exhaustion recovery is helpful but modest, and Vigil offers a stronger support effect that can also help nearby teammates.
Ghost Notes therefore makes sense when the user specifically wants the combination of Exhaustion support and trail disruption. As a general slot, its impact is too small for the upper tiers.
editorial.verdict: A useful but modest Exhaustion companion. Ghost Notes adds passive trail disruption and a little recovery speed, but rarely changes a match by itself.
